title: Bigger, better, different
description: Compare things, and say what should happen.
grammarNote: Más and menos compare. The superlative adds -ísimo: el más grande, la más pequeña.

explanation.summary: Comparing two things uses más, menos, mejor and peor. Saying which one is the biggest of a set uses the superlative, and the most useful form is the short one: más grande, not el más grande.

sections.heading: Two things
sections.body: For the adjectives that can take it, the comparison is más or menos plus the adjective: más grande, menos caro. For a small set of adjectives the comparative has its own word: mejor, peor, más, menos. And the comparison uses than, which is que: es más grande que el mío.

examples.es: Esta casa es más grande que la otra.
examples.en: This house is bigger than the other one.

examples.es: Este café es mejor que aquel.
examples.en: This coffee is better than that one.

examples.es: Es más barato de lo que parece.
examples.en: It is cheaper than it looks.

sections.heading: The most of a set
sections.body: To say which one is the biggest of a group, you do not need an article: el más grande becomes simply más grande. The word for the group goes after: el más grande de los libros. The intensifier -ísimo is another way to say it, and it is stronger: grandísimo, the very biggest.

examples.es: Es el más grande de los almacenes.
examples.en: It is the biggest of the storerooms.

examples.es: Es el más grande de la clase.
examples.en: It is the biggest in the class.

sections.heading: Equal, and not equal
sections.body: Equality uses tan plus an adjective plus como: es tan alto como tú. Inequality can also be expressed with como with tan: no es tan alto como tú. And an equal comparison of two nouns uses igual de: es igual de grande.

examples.en: He is as tall as you.

examples.es: No es tan caro como el otro.
examples.en: It is not as expensive as the other one.

items.note: More. It also means most. It takes an accent in a question.
Better. It has no comparative form: es mejor, es el mejor.
Worse. Like mejor, it never changes.
Higher, superior. It also means better.
Lower, inferior. It also means worse.
Main, most important. It does not change for a feminine noun.
Special. It does not change for a feminine noun.
Strong. It does not change for a feminine noun.
Soft, smooth. It does not change for a feminine noun.

drills.prompt: Esta casa es ___ grande que la otra.
drills.meaning: this house is bigger than the other one
drills.note: Más plus the adjective, then que.

drills.meaning: it is the biggest in the class
this coffee is better than that one
he is as tall as you

drills.prompt: No es ___ caro como el otro.
drills.meaning: it is not as expensive as the other one
drills.note: Inequality also uses tan plus como.
